title: Adaptive dependency throttling and region-aware failover for cache and streaming stores
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement an adaptive throttling and region-aware failover strategy for critical downstream stores (Redis, Kafka, Postgres) to protect the serving runtime SLOs under partial outages or degradation. Deliverables: a) token-bucket and slow-start backoff for per-connection pools, b) hysteresis-aware circuit breakers with asymmetric open/close thresholds, c) region-aware routing with graceful fallback policies, and d) degradations modes (stale-cache, embed-only, read-only) with clear telemetry and runbook hooks.
background: Recent incidents during cross-region network blips and Kafka broker flaps showed cascading timeouts from Redis and increased tail latency on the inference path. On 2026-02-19 an overloaded Redis shard caused request queues to grow and connection pools to exhaust, producing 3minute service degradations and repeated customer complaints. Current behavior: callers retry aggressively, causing amplification; circuit breakers are binary and slow to recover; connection pools lack per-tenant adaptability.
proposal: We propose a multi-layer protection scheme: (1) lightweight client-side rate shaping per upstream (token-bucket with dynamic refill tuned to observed healthy QPS), (2) small adaptive connection sub-pools per AZ with prioritized fast-paths and a cold-path that returns degraded responses, (3) circuit breakers with hysteresis and progressive throttling (50% -> 25% -> 0% fast-pass windows) instead of immediate blackhole, (4) region-aware failover: prefer local-region reads, on local degradation route to warm replica region with fanout limit, (5) controlled load-shedding policies exposed to caller with structured error types indicating degradations so clients can fall back to cached or best-effort flows.
implementation_steps: Instrument current upstreams to emit per-connection QPS, p95/p99 latency, and error budget burn-rate (2 days)
Prototype token-bucket rate shaper in serving runtime and toggle via feature-flag (1 week)
Implement hysteresis circuit breaker library with asymmetric open/close thresholds and gradual throttling windows (2 weeks)
Add region-aware routing policy that can consult health signals and enforce fanout and capacity budgets per region (1 week)
Implement degraded response modes for cache misses (stale TTL, embed-only, metadata-only) and make them pluggable per route (1 week)
End-to-end load tests with synthetic Redis/Kafka failure injection and chaos scenarios, validate SLO preservation (3 days)
Rollout in canary with runtime-2.4 for low-QPS tenants, monitor, then ramp to broader traffic (3 days)
Post-mortem and refine thresholds based on observed trade-offs (1 week)
acceptance_criteria: Under controlled upstream degradation (simulated 50% increased latency on Redis), platform request success SLO (99.5% p50/p90 within latency targets) remains within target for 30 minutes
Circuit breakers transition through progressive throttling windows instead of immediate full open, and recover automatically when health metrics return to baseline
Region-aware failover reduces cross-region fanout by at least 40% compared to current naive failover during local region outage
Degraded response modes returnStructured error codes and clear telemetry showing when and why a request was degraded
No customer-visible increase in error rates for non-impacted tenants during canary rollout
monitoring_playbook: Define SLOs: 99.5% successful responses within 120ms for local cache hits; 99% within 300ms for reads involving warm replica regions
Alerts: (1) Upstream error-rate > 1% sustained for 2 minutes, (2) Pool exhaustion > 80% for 1 minute, (3) Circuit-breaker open-rate > 5% overall traffic

Runbook: On pool exhaustion alert, reduce non-critical traffic routes by 30% via dynamic route-weighting and enable degraded-mode responses; if broken, perform regional traffic shift to cold replica region
Dashboards: per-region per-upstream heatmaps (QPS, p50/p95/p99 latency, pool usage), circuit breaker state over time, degradation counts by route
Post-incident steps: capture cause, adjust bucket sizes, tweak circuit thresholds, and add replay tests to CI
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated: default off for all tenants
Enable for internal infra traffic and low-QPS tenants in a single region (canary) for 48 hours
If canary passes, enable adaptive throttling only for 10% of production routes for 72 hours
Gradually enable region-aware failover for read-heavy routes over a two-week window
Full rollout after two successful incident-free weeks and sign-off from SRE and PL
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive shedding could drop legitimate traffic. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds and quick rollback via feature flags
Risk: Increased complexity in routing may cause new edge cases. Mitigation: smoke tests and chaos injections in staging before rollout
Risk: Clients misinterpret structured degraded responses. Mitigation: publish client contract with error codes and provide SDK helpers to surface fallbacks
Risk: Cross-region traffic costs increase during failover. Mitigation: enforce fanout caps and billing alarms
notes: Related incident: INC-2026-02-19-redis-shard-exhaustion (postmortem linked in Confluence)
